children: New Zealand's benchmark NZX-50 index falls 0.5% to 13931.39 soon after opening as investors adjust to political uncertainty after Saturday's election had no clear winner. The ruling National Party and its right-wing allies had 67 seats after 100% of the election-day vote was counted. But hundreds of thousands of so-called special votes still must be counted. In past elections, these have reduced National's seat count. PM Luxon and opposition leader Hipkins both said the election was too close to call. Coalition talks with minor parties may be needed to decide the next government. Tourism Holdings and Air New Zealand lead early rises, up 2.1% and 1.3%, respectively. Ryman Healthcare falls 2.2% and Fisher & Paykel Healthcare drops 1.7%. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
